title: Award-size sanity - a fund whose minimum dwarfs the goal must not headline
provenance: Briefing v2 regression, 8 Jul 2026: the £500k-£5m National Lottery 'UK Fund' headlined a £150k cash goal (CGK). Selection needs an award-size compatibility dimension: a minimum award larger than the remaining gap is wrong advice regardless of sector fit, and must be demoted (named if it still surfaces).

expected.judge_guidance: The oversized national fund is a perfect sector match but its minimum award (£500,000) is more than four times the £120,000 goal, so recommending it is wrong advice and fails the consultant test. A good readout leads with the right-sized fund, keeps the whole agenda proportionate to a £120k goal, and if the oversized fund surfaces at all names the mismatch plainly (minimum award larger than the whole goal) rather than presenting it as a headline opportunity.

notes: Regression guard for the award-size compatibility dimension added to selection in briefing v2. The oversized fixture is deliberately fully ELIGIBLE (no income floor/ceiling that would rule it out), so only the award-size sanity demotes it - isolating the dimension under test.
